title.value: Network-based Active Inference and its Application in Robotics

abstract.value: This paper introduces Network-based Active Inference (NetAIF), a novel robotic framework that enables real-time learning and adaptability in dynamic, unstructured environments. NetAIF leverages random attractor dynamics and the Free Energy Principle (FEP) to simplify trajectory generation through network-topology-driven attractors that induce controlled instabilities and probabilistic sampling cycles. This approach allows robots to efficiently adapt to changing conditions without requiring extensive pre-training or pre-calculated trajectories. By integrating learning and control mechanisms within a compact model architecture, NetAIF facilitates seamless task execution, such as target tracking and valve manipulation. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments demonstrate NetAIF's capability to perform rapid and precise real-time adjustments, highlighting its suitability for applications requiring high adaptability and efficient control, such as robotics tasks in the energy and manufacturing sectors.
